description: A two-channel oscilloscope built for envelopes, with movable indices for measuring a time span and a voltage.

params.text: Sets the vertical scaling of that channel's trace on the screen.
Moves that channel's trace up and down the screen, -10V to +10V.
Sets the voltage the trigger fires at, -10V to +10V.
Sets how long a stretch of time one sweep of the screen covers.
Moves the left vertical index across the screen; the span between the two indices is shown as a time.
Moves the right vertical index across the screen; the span between the two indices is shown as a time.
Moves the horizontal index up and down the screen; the voltage at that level is shown for each channel.
Switches between tracing continuously and taking a single sweep and holding it.
Starts and stops tracing; with its light out the last trace stays on the screen.
Sets how much of the 100-sample pre-trigger buffer is drawn before the trigger point, which is marked by a red vertical line.
Chooses how that channel is drawn: a CV signal traced as a single line, or an audio signal rectified and filled in to show the peak across a short window of samples.

inputs.text: The first channel traced; it also triggers the sweep unless something is patched into the external trigger input.
Triggers the sweep on a rising edge through the LEVEL setting whenever anything is patched here, and is not itself traced.

notes: the screen is swept on a trigger, so nothing is drawn until a signal rises through the LEVEL setting: the A channel's own signal, or whatever is patched into the external trigger input.
a small blue light flashes on each trigger; if it is dark, either the signal is not rising through the LEVEL setting or the RUN button is off.
with the CONT/ONCE switch at ONCE, press RUN to arm a sweep; one trace is taken at the next trigger edge and the screen then holds it.
menu: Match Cable Colors — draws each trace in the colour of the cable patched into it.
Visuals — a submenu of Blue, Dark and Light for the colour scheme, plus Flat for a look without the 3D shading. The choice covers every SubmarineFree module and is kept outside the patch.
